note: The same question written three ways. `unaccent` is applied to the query exactly as it was applied to the text at write time (docs/PLAN.md §6.2), so an accent-stripped or upper-cased query must reach the same articles in the same order. A drop here is a normalisation bug, not a relevance opinion — which is why it is reported as agreement against the reference variant rather than folded into nDCG.

cases.query: indemnité de licenciement et condition d'ancienneté
cases.note: Reference form, correctly accented, mixed case.

cases.query: INDEMNITE DE LICENCIEMENT ET CONDITION D'ANCIENNETE
cases.note: Upper case and unaccented — how text pasted out of a scanned pleading or an OCR layer usually arrives.

cases.query: congés payés durée du congé annuel du salarié
cases.note: Reference form. 'Congés payés' is the highest-frequency accented phrase in French employment law, so it is the right probe for the unaccent path.

cases.query: conges payes duree du conge annuel du salarie
cases.note: Fully unaccented lower case — the form a lawyer types on a keyboard set to another layout, and the one that breaks a naive tsvector setup outright.

cases.query: harcèlement moral dégradation des conditions de travail
Harcelement Moral Degradation Des Conditions De Travail
cases.note: Title case and unaccented at once — the two normalisation axes combined.

cases.query: référé prud'homal créance non sérieusement contestable
cases.note: Reference form. Three accented words plus an apostrophe, which is the other tokenisation hazard.

cases.query: refere prud'homal creance non serieusement contestable
cases.note: Unaccented. 'refere' also happens to be a valid French word form, so this variant additionally checks that stripping accents does not change the stem the french configuration picks.
